question_text: When a hypothetical metal having a grain diameter of \(8.2 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{~mm}\) is heated to \(500^{\circ} \mathrm{C}\) for 12.5 min , the grain diameter increases to \(2.7 \times 10^{-2} \mathrm{~mm}\). Compute the grain diameter when a specimen of the original material is heated at \(500^{\circ} \mathrm{C}\) for 100 min . Assume the grain diameter exponent \(n\) has a value of 2.The unit of the answer is mm.
